text.p: Kvaerner, the Norwegian international engineering and construction group, announced on Friday that Peter Ward, a director of Kvaerner PLC and chairman and chief executive of Cunard cruise line, had resigned.

Ward, who is based at Cunard's headquarters in New York, has decided to return to London to pursue other interests and will leave the group at the end of October, a statement issued by Kvaerner's London headquarters said.
He is being replaced by Antti Pankakoski, currently vice-president of Kvaerner's shipbuilding business area.

Pankakoski, who will take up his new position on November 1, has spent 16 years in the shipbuilding industry, five of which have been with the Kvaerner group. Most recently he was executive vice-president of Kvaerner Masa-Yards in Finland.

Erik Tonseth, president and CEO of Kvaerner said: "Antti Pankakoski brings broad experience of working with the cruise industry and will continue to drive Cunard's re-organisation programme. The group is fully supportive of Cunard's objectives to re-focus the company's activities in the luxury cruise market, and to achieve its goal of producing future sustainable profit levels".
